thread:
maria (eng-security): Heads-up: customer ACME on Private deployed stack reported possible cross-namespace access. Audit shows a serviceAccount from ns=shared calling Secrets in ns=customer-42.
kevin (eng-platform): ugh. any pointers in the audit logs?
audit-bot: Found event: user=system:serviceaccount:shared:shared-sa verb=get resource=secrets namespace=customer-42 requestURI=/api/v1/namespaces/customer-42/secrets/db-creds status=200
sophie (eng-sre): timeline? when did this start?
maria (eng-security): first hit 2024-11-02T08:12:05Z in the audit stream, multiple accesses over 45m. last seen ~2024-11-02T08:57:10Z.
taylor (customer-success): Customer noticed credentials access anomalies in their app and opened a support ticket. They've paused traffic to that tenant for now.
kevin (eng-platform): Possible causes: 1) shared namespace got overly-permissive ClusterRoleBinding 2) NetworkPolicy allowed pod-to-pod traffic across namespaces (we allow intra-cluster by default in some private bundles) 3) serviceAccount token mounted in workload with broad permissions.
maria (eng-security): Agreed. Immediate mitigations we can do now: revoke any wildcard CRBs, isolate the nodepool via taints/labels, and apply temporary deny-everything NetworkPolicy for customer-42.
sophie (eng-sre): I can revoke CRBs. Which binding name to remove?
maria (eng-security): Run: ```bash
kubectl get clusterrolebinding -o wide | egrep "shared|devops|wildcard" 
# look for entries binding system:serviceaccounts to cluster-admin
kubectl delete clusterrolebinding shared-cluster-admin-binding
```
kevin (eng-platform): Also do `kubectl get rolebinding --all-namespaces -o wide | grep shared-sa` — there might be a namespace-scoped RoleBinding elevating it.
taylor (customer-success): I'll coordinate with ACME on the change window and confirm they want us to revoke now; they approved immediate revocation.
maria (eng-security): After CRB removal: apply a scoped NetworkPolicy on customer-42 to deny ingress/egress except from explicit service accounts. Example: ```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-all-except-allowed
  namespace: customer-42
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
  ingress: []
  egress: []
```
sophie (eng-sre): We should avoid a complete lockout. We'll apply `deny-all-except-allowed` then add allowed rules for the customer's own SA + monitoring hook.
kevin (eng-platform): For Private deployments on VPC, also push a VPC-level control: restrict cross-subnet routes and ensure no overly-broad security groups allowing cluster-crossover. On-prem: check iptables/OVS rules on the affected nodes.
maria (eng-security): Next: audit logging and forensic. We need to snapshot the etcd and kube-apiserver audit logs ASAP and preserve KMS-wrapped envelopes. Also start a timeline for incident response (ICS-2024-112).
audit-bot: Exporting audit slice to /forensics/ICS-2024-112/audit-1712345678.tar.gz (encrypted).
sophie (eng-sre): Forensics tasks: 1) collect pod manifests for shared-sa 2) collect node logs 3) list process pulls and images for suspicious containers 4) check mount points for tokens 5) snapshot pvc volumes if possible.
maria (eng-security): KMS notes: customer-ACME uses customer-managed key (CMK) for audit envelope encryption. We need to rotate the CMK or put it in pending rotation after we ensure decrypts for forensics. Proposed: create a new key, re-encrypt the audit archive, then schedule old key for rotation with a hold period.
kevin (eng-platform): Command pattern (generic): ```bash
kms-cli rewrap --src-key "arn:cmk:ACME:old-key" --dest-key "arn:cmk:ACME:new-key" /forensics/ICS-2024-112/audit-1712345678.tar.gz
kms-cli rotate --key arn:cmk:ACME:old-key --defer-days 7
```
kevin (eng-platform): We can't destroy old key until legal/forensics sign-off. hold = yes.
maria (eng-security): RBAC long-term fix: run a sweep to ensure no roleBindings/clusterRoleBindings grant `*` verbs or bind `system:serviceaccounts` to cluster-admin. Suggested policy: deny bindings that include `subjects: - kind: Group name: system:serviceaccounts` at PR time in our admission checks.
sophie (eng-sre): We'll push an admission webhook rule to block new CRBs binding system:serviceaccounts to cluster-admin. Quick snippet for the policy in our repo: `reject-if-subjects-include-system-serviceaccounts`.
taylor (customer-success): ACME asked about isolation SLA and guarantees — can we give them a short note? They want to know whether private deployments are tenant-siloed by default.
maria (eng-security): Short answer: by default we provide logical isolation (namespaces, RBAC) and recommend NetworkPolicy + VPC segmentation for stronger guarantees. We're updating docs to make the default-safe posture explicit and will create a hardened profile for tenant-siloed installs.
kevin (eng-platform): Action items assigned: Sophie to revoke CRB & apply NetworkPolicy (in next 15m). Maria to lead forensics and RBAC sweep. Kevin to prepare KMS rewrap and coordinate with infra for VPC rule lockdown. Taylor to keep ACME informed.
sophie (eng-sre): Done: `kubectl delete clusterrolebinding shared-cluster-admin-binding` (applied) — verified no immediate crashes. Applied initial NetworkPolicy allowed-only rules; customer confirmed services still reachable.
audit-bot: Audit slice uploaded to secure bucket; access ACL set to forensics+sre+security only.
maria (eng-security): For tracking: opened ICS ticket ICS-2024-112, severity P2 (customer data exposure). Forensics ETA: 6 hours initial, full report 48-72 hours.
taylor (customer-success): ACME acknowledged steps and appreciates the fast action. They want follow-up on root cause and remediation timeline.
kevin (eng-platform): Root cause hypothesis for post-incident: a deployment script created a namespace-scoped RoleBinding for `shared-sa` but a subsequent automation promoted it to a ClusterRoleBinding via templated overlay — rollout of a config change with `apply --prune` that matched resource name. We'll add lints to the templating pipeline to prevent accidental promotion.
maria (eng-security): Postmortem checklist items: - confirm all affected secrets rotated - publish customer-facing summary - add CI policy to block CRBs binding system:serviceaccounts - create hardened private-deploy profile - test networkpolicy defaults in canary clusters
sophie (eng-sre): Also monitor for any other serviceAccounts in `shared` namespace with nonstandard bindings: `kubectl get rolebinding,clusterrolebinding --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.subjects[]? | .name=="shared-sa")'`
maria (eng-security): Closing loop: do not rotate or delete CMKs until forensics confirms. Keep audit archives immutable for now.
taylor (customer-success): I'll log the timeline with ACME and schedule a postmortem call tomorrow.
kevin (eng-platform): I'm going to add an automated nightly job to scan for CRBs that bind `system:serviceaccounts` and open tickets for any matches.
kevin (eng-platform): Also note: we should document allowed attack surface in private deploy README — clarifying what we consider "soft isolation" vs. hardened tenant-silo.
maria (eng-security): Thanks team. If anything else shows up from the logs, ping here. We'll publish the incident summary after forensics. :lock:
